readings.title: The Search for Qish's Donkeys
readings.subtitle: Sha’ul is Led to the Seer
readings.text: [1 Samuel 9:1] And there was a man of Binyamin whose name was Qish, son of Aḇi’ĕl, son of Tseror, son of Beḵorath, son of Aphiyaḥ, a Binyamite, a mighty man of power. [2] And he had a son whose name was Sha’ul, young and handsome. And there was not a more handsome man than he among the children of Yisra’ĕl, taller than any of the people by the shoulders and upwards. [3] And the donkeys of Qish, father of Sha’ul, were lost. And Qish said to his son Sha’ul, “Please take <dn>את</dn> one of the servants with <dn>את</dn> you, and arise, go seek <dn>את</dn> the donkeys.” [4] And he passed through the mountains of Ephrayim and through <dn>את</dn> the land of Shalishah, but they did not find them. Then they passed through the land of Sha‘alim, but they were not. Then he passed through the land of the Binyamites, but they did not find them. [5] They came to the land of Tsuph, and Sha’ul said to his servant who was with <dn>את</dn> him, “Come, let us turn back, lest my father stops thinking about the donkeys and become worried about us.” [6] And he said to him, “See, there is in this city a man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the man is esteemed. All that he says comes true, without fail. Now, let us go there. It could be that he shows us <dn>את</dn> our way to go.” [7] And Sha’ul said to his servant, “But look, if we go, what do we bring the man? For the bread in our bags is all gone, and there is no present to bring to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>. What do we have?” [8] And the servant answered <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul again and said, “Look, I have here at hand one fourth of a sheqel of silver. And I shall give that to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and he shall make known to us <dn>את</dn> our way.” [9] Formerly, in Yisra’ĕl, when a man went to inquire of <dn>Elohim</dn>, he spoke thus, “Come, let us go to the seer,” for the prophet of today was formerly called a seer. [10] And Sha’ul said to his servant, “Your word is good. Come, let us go.” And they went to the city where the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> was. [11] As they went up the hill to the city, they met some young women going out to draw water, and said to them, “Is the seer here?” [12] And they answered them and said, “He is. Look, ahead of you. Hurry now, for he came to this city today, for the people have a slaughtering on the high place today. [13] “As you come into the city, you are going to find <dn>את</dn> him before he goes up to the high place to eat. For the people do not eat until he comes, for he blesses the slaughtering, afterward they who are invited eat. And now, go up, for you should find <dn>את</dn> him about this time.” [14] And they went up to the city. They were coming into the midst of the city, and saw Shemu’ĕl coming out toward them to go up to the high place.

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Decree to Shemu’el
readings.subtitle: The Leader for the Counter-Offensive
readings.text: [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had revealed to <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl in his ear the day before Sha’ul came, saying, [16] <dq>At this time tomorrow <dn>I</dn> shall send you a man from the land of Binyamin, and you shall anoint <dn>את</dn> him leader over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and he shall save <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people from the hand of the Philistines. For <dn>I</dn> have seen <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people, because their cry has come to <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [17] And when Shemu’ĕl saw <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>See, the man of whom <dn>I</dn> spoke to you. Let this one govern <dn>My</dn> people.</dq>

readings.title: The Seer’s Feast for Sha’ul
readings.subtitle: Elevating the Least of Binyamin
readings.text: [18] And Sha’ul drew near to <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl in the gate, and said, “Please inform me, where is the house of the seer?” [19] And Shemu’ĕl answered <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul and said, “I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with <dn>את</dn> me today. And tomorrow I shall let you go and make known to you <dn>את</dn> all that is in your heart. [20] “As for your donkeys that were lost three days ago, do not set <dn>את</dn> your heart on them, for they have been found. And on whom is all the desire of Yisra’ĕl? Is it not on you and on all your father’s house?” [21] And Sha’ul answered and said, “Am I not a Binyamite – of the smallest of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, and my clan the least of all the clans of the tribe of Binyamin? Why then do you speak like this to me?” [22] And Shemu’ĕl took <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul and <dn>את</dn> his servant and brought them into the hall, and gave to them a place at the head of those who were invited, and there were about thirty men. [23] And Shemu’ĕl said to the cook, “Bring <dn>את</dn> the portion which I gave you, of which I told you to set it aside.” [24] And the cook brought out <dn>את</dn> the thigh with its upper part and set it before Sha’ul. And Shemu’ĕl said, “See what was kept back. It was set aside for you. Eat, for it has been kept for you for this appointed time, saying, I have invited <dn>את</dn> the people.” And Sha’ul ate with <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl on that day. [25] And they came down from the high place into the city, and Shemu’ĕl spoke with <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul on the roof. [26] And they rose early. And it came to be about the dawning of the day that Shemu’ĕl called to Sha’ul on the roof, saying, “Rise, so that I send you on your way.” And Sha’ul rose, and both of them went outside, he and Shemu’ĕl. [27] As they were walking toward the edge of the city, Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “Say to the servant to go on ahead of us.” And he went on. “But you stand here a moment, so that I let you hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>Elohim</dn>.”

readings.title: The Ammonite Ultimatum
readings.subtitle: A Demand for the Right Eye
readings.text: [1 Samuel 11:1] And Naḥash the Ammonite came up and camped against Yaḇĕsh Gil‘aḏ. And all the men of Yaḇĕsh said to Naḥash, “Make a covenant with us, and we shall serve you.” [2] Then Naḥash the Ammonite answered them, “For this I make a covenant with you, that I dig out all your right eyes, and I shall bring reproach on all Yisra’ĕl.” [3] And the elders of Yaḇĕsh said to him, “Leave us alone for seven days, so that we send messengers to all the borders of Yisra’ĕl. And then, if there is no one to save us, we shall come out to you.” [4] And the messengers came to Giḇ‘ah of Sha’ul and spoke <dn>את</dn> the words in the hearing of the people. And all the people lifted up <dn>את</dn> their voices and wept. [5] And look, Sha’ul was coming behind the herd from the field. And Sha’ul said, “Why are the people weeping?” And they related to him <dn>את</dn> the words of the men of Yaḇĕsh.

readings.section: The Power of the Right Arm
readings.title: The Spirit Rouses Sha’ul
readings.subtitle: Gathering the Host of Yisra’ĕl
readings.text: [6] And the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon Sha’ul mightily as he heard <dn>את</dn> these words, and his displeasure burned greatly. [7] And he took a yoke of cattle and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the border of Yisra’ĕl by the hands of messengers, saying, “Whoever does not go out with Sha’ul and Shemu’ĕl to battle, let this be done to his cattle.” And the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> fell on the people, and they came out as one man. [8] And he mustered them in Bezeq, and the children of Yisra’ĕl were three hundred thousand, and the men of Yehuḏah thirty thousand. [9] And they said to the messengers who came, “Say this to the men of Yaḇĕsh Gil‘aḏ, ‘Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have help.’ ” Then the messengers came and informed <dn>את</dn> the men of Yaḇĕsh, and they rejoiced. [10] So the men of Yaḇĕsh said, “Tomorrow we come out to you, and you shall do to us whatever seems good to you.” [11] And it came to be, on the next day, that Sha’ul put <dn>את</dn> the people in three companies. And they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch and struck <dn>את</dn> Ammon until the heat of the day. And it came to be that those left were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.

readings.title: Mercy and the Renewal at Gilgal
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Wrought Deliverance
readings.text: [12] And the people said to Shemu’ĕl, “Who said, ‘Shall Sha’ul reign over us?’ Bring the men, so that we put them to death.” [13] But Sha’ul said, “No man is put to death this day, for today <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has wrought deliverance in Yisra’ĕl.” [14] And Shemu’ĕl said to the people, “Come, and let us go to Gilgal and renew <dn>את</dn> the reign there.” [15] And all the people went to Gilgal, and there they set up <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul to reign before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Gilgal, and there they slaughtered slaughterings of peace offerings before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And there Sha’ul rejoiced, and all the men of Yisra’ĕl, very greatly.

readings.title: A Witness Before YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The Rejection of Bribes and Oppression
readings.text: [1 Samuel 12:1] And Shemu’ĕl said to all Yisra’ĕl, “Look, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and have set a sovereign over you. [2] “And now, look, the sovereign is walking before you. And I am old and grey, and look, my sons are with <dn>את</dn> you. And I have walked before you from my youth to this day. [3] “Look, here I am. Witness against me before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and before <dn>His</dn> anointed: Whose ox have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken, or <dn>את</dn> whom have I oppressed? <dn>את</dn> Whom have I abused, or from whose hand have I received any bribe with which to blind my eyes? – then I restore it to you.” [4] And they said, “You have not oppressed us or abused us, nor have you taken any bribe from anyone’s hand.” [5] So he said to them, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is witness against you, and <dn>His</dn> anointed is witness today, that you have found naught in my hand.” And they answered, “<dn>He</dn> is witness.”

readings.title: The Cycle of Rebellion and Grace
readings.subtitle: Forgetting YeHoVaH the Sovereign
readings.text: [6] And Shemu’ĕl said to the people, “It is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who appointed <dn>את</dn> Mosheh and <dn>את</dn> Aharon, and who brought <dn>את</dn> your fathers up from the land of Mitsrayim. [7] “And now, stand still, so that I judge <dn>את</dn> you before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning all the righteous acts of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> did to <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> your fathers: [8] “When Ya‘aqoḇ had come to Mitsrayim, and your fathers cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> Mosheh and <dn>את</dn> Aharon, who brought <dn>את</dn> your fathers out of Mitsrayim and made them dwell in this place. [9] “But they forgot <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, so <dn>He</dn> sold <dn>את</dn> them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Ḥatsor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the sovereign of Mo’aḇ. And they fought against them. [10] “And they cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and served <dn>את</dn> the Ba‘als and <dn>את</dn> the Ashtaroth. And now, deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we serve <dn>You</dn>.’ [11] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> Yerubba‘al, and <dn>את</dn> Beḏan, and <dn>את</dn> Yiphtaḥ, and <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl, and delivered <dn>את</dn> you out of the hand of your enemies round about, and you dwelt in safety. [12] “And when you saw that Naḥash sovereign of the children of Ammon came against you, you said to me, ‘No, but let a sovereign reign over us,’ when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> was your sovereign.

readings.title: Thunder in the Wheat Harvest
readings.subtitle: A Visible Display of Divine Displeasure
readings.text: [13] “And now, here is the sovereign whom you have chosen and whom you have asked. And see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has set a sovereign over you. [14] “If you fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and shall serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn> and obey <dn>His</dn> voice, and not rebel against <dn>את</dn> the command of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then both you and the sovereign who reigns over you shall follow <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [15] “But if you do not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and shall rebel against <dn>את</dn> the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be against you, as it was against your fathers. [16] “And now, stand and see <dn>את</dn> this great matter which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does before your eyes: [17] “Is today not the wheat harvest? Let me call to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, so that <dn>He</dn> sends thunder and rain – know then and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in asking for yourselves a sovereign.” [18] And Shemu’ĕl called to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent thunder and rain that day. And all the people greatly feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl.

readings.title: A Call to Fear and Serve in Truth
readings.subtitle: The Danger of Worthless Matters
readings.text: [19] And all the people said to Shemu’ĕl, “Pray for your servants to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, that we do not die, for we have added to all our sins this evil of asking for ourselves a sovereign.” [20] And Shemu’ĕl said to the people, “Do not fear. You have done <dn>את</dn> all this evil. Only, do not turn aside from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And you shall serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with all your heart, [21] and do not turn aside after worthless matters which do not profit or deliver, for they are worthless. [22] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would not cast away <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> people, for <dn>His</dn> great Name’s sake, seeing it has pleased <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to make <dn>את</dn> you <dn>His</dn> people. [23] “Also, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in ceasing to pray for you, but I shall teach <dn>את</dn> you the good and straight way. [24] “Only fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and you shall serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn> in truth with all your heart, for consider <dn>את</dn> what marvels <dn>He</dn> has done for you. [25] “But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your sovereign are consumed.”
